claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- Iran says it will wait for official US response after Trump rejects Strait of Hormuz proposal: The US president earlier said that Tehran only made the proposal to open the strait within seven days because "they're losing so badly".
- Christa Pike to be first woman executed in Tennessee in 200 years - but her defence say she's a victim too: Lawyers for Pike, who killed a fellow student in 1995, say she should get clemency and would not be sentenced to death if the crime happened today.
- Four killed in helicopter crash near Montreal: The victims of the crash have not yet been identified, Quebec provincial police told the BBC.
- Pope praises young people's 'energy and commitment' at huge open-air Mass in Paris: Around 700,000 people gathered in central Paris to hear the Catholic leader speak and offer prayer.
- British national among six dead in building explosion close to Acropolis in Athens: Four Americans and a Greek national are among those killed in a suspected gas explosion, officials said.
- German town bans 'stumbling stone' memorials to Nazi victims: Germany's education minister has branded the ban on the small brass memorial plaques a "scandal".
- Nor'easter brings flooding as New York and New Jersey declare emergency: Tens of millions of people from Maine to Virginia are in the path of the powerful storm.
- Republic of Ireland to wear black armbands for Israel game: Republic of Ireland players intend to wear black armbands "in recognition of all lives lost in the [Gaza] conflict" for match against Israel.
- Mother of woman found hanging in tree shocked as police say body was staged: Christy Spivey tells the BBC she only has more questions now police think Tasia Fortune's body was put in the tree after her death.
- Bangkok roads submerged as flood disaster declared: Authorities said the heavy rains have subsided but the flooding is not yet over.
- Security lapses at Utah campus where Charlie Kirk was killed, review says: The independent report also says Kirk's aides insisted he speak outdoors, overriding concerns from campus officials.
- Brazil's Lula bans online gambling ahead of presidential election: Lula, who is currently in a tight presidential race against Flávio Bolsonaro, said the industry was a "cancer" that he must "remove".
